recall all what has been taught in the previous term.

Living and Non Living Things

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1, WEEK 1 - WEEK 6
WEEK 1 | WEEK 2 - LIVING LIVING THINGS AT HOME AND IN THE SCHOOL
Living things are things that are alive. Living things breath in and out. They need air, food or water. They can move, grow and reproduce. For example, people, plants and animals.
Anything that walk, eat and drink, talk or make sound, grow, defecate and die are living things.
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to -
1. Mention 5 living things in the school compound.
2. State 5 living things at compound.
WEEK 3 - NON LIVING AT HOME AND IN THE SCHOOL
Non living things are things that are not alive. They do not need air, food or water. They do not move.
They do not grow and do not reproduce. For example, books, chairs and desks, etc.
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask the pupils state 5 non living things in the classroom.
WEEK 4 | WEEK 5 | WEEK 6 - EXPLORING THE ENVIRONMENT
Exploring is the walking around in a new environment to learn, search or discover new things. Exploring the environment involved walking along the roads and there are different types of road.
There are a lot things that can be found when exploring an environment or walking along the road (across the road). For example, houses, cars, trees, boats, animals, etc.
Road can be a private roads, community roads, district roads, state roads or federal roads. These roads depend on who built the roads.
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to -
1. Explain what exploring the environment means.
2. State 5 types of roads.
3. Mention 5 things that can found when exploring the roads.
LESSON 2, WEEK 7 - WEEK 11
WEEK 7 | WEEK 8 - COLOURS AND ITS USES
Colour is a appearance of things in a unique reflection.
For example, Nigerian flag is Green White Green. It is used for logo, identity, traffic light, dye, beautification, decoration, design, writing, drawing, etc.
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to identify colours on some collected objects or logo.
WEEK 9 | WEEK 10 - TRAFFIC LIGHTS AND COLOURS
Road traffic lights sign are lights used to control the movement of traffic. They are placed on roads. The different colors of lights tell drivers what to do. For example, Red - Go, Yellow - READY TO GO and Green - GO
LESSON EVALUATION
State the functions of each of the following road traffic signs - Red, Yellow and Green.
WEEK 11 - ROAD MAKINGS AND COLOURS
Road markings are lines that define the directions and activities of road users. There are two (2) major colours used on the roads - Black and White.
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to mention 2 major road marking colours.

2. Discuss each lessons of first term’s work.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
EXPLORING THE SCHOOL IMMEDIATE ENVIRONMENT
Take the pupils for a walk within the environment. Guide them to identify and state some of the basic features within the school environment.
MEANING OF EXPLORING
Exploring the environment is the walking around in a new environment to learn, search or discover new things.
TYPES OF ROAD
1. Private roads
2. Community roads
3. District roads
4. Federal roads
LESSON 2 - TYPES OF ROAD WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE SCHOOL
Exploring the environment involved walking along the roads and there are different types of road -
1. Private roads
Road within or inside the school. Access to these is restricted from non members.
2. Community Roads
These roads are built by the communities to access to their resident or farmlands.
3. District Roads
These roads constructed and managed by the communities or local government authorities.
These roads are known as Truck C. The roads link one street to another within the local government.
3. State Roads
These roads are constructed and managed by the state government. The roads connected from local together. They are known as Truck B and bigger than the local government roads.
4. Federal Roads
These are wider roads that connect all states in Nigeria together. These roads shared borders with neighbouring countries. They are known as Truck A.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Takes pupils on a study walk around and outside the school to explore different types of toads in their environment.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe and identify different types of roads
3. Leads a discussion on the meaning of exploring and types of roads.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
4. Summarizes each lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Exploring Your Environment - Walking Along and Across The road (Primary 1)

Ask pupils to:
1. meaning of exploring.
2. identify types of roads around the school and roads outside the school.

1. _______ roads restricted access to non members.
A. Private roads
B. Community roads
C. District roads
2. _______ roads give access to the people in a community.
A. Private roads
B. Community roads
C. District roads
3. _______ roads connected different streets together within a community.
A. Private roads
B. Community roads
C. District roads
4. _______ roads connected all local government areas within the state.
A. Local government roads
B. State roads
C. Federal  roads
5. _______ roads connected all states together.
A. Local government roads
B. State roads
C. Federal  roads

topics.title: Living Things: Meaning and Examples of Living Things, and Living Things in the School Environment | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 1 Basic Science and Technology
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (BST)
PRIMARY 1 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME - LIVING THINGS
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - LIVING THINGS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Examples of Living Things
3. Living Things in the school and Caring for Living Things
4. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Say what living things are.
2. Mention examples of living things.
3. Identify living things in the school.
4. Name some plants and animals found in the school.
5. State one way to care for living things.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils can identify familiar plants, animals and people around them.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
Pictures of people, plants and animals
1. Real leaves and flowers
2. Picture cards, Charts
3. Objects found around the school
4. Writing board
METHOD OF TEACHING
The teacher uses observation, demonstration, questioning, discussion, identification, repetition and simple practical activities.
The teacher begins by showing pupils pictures of a person, a plant and an animal and asking them to identify what they can see.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Lagos State Scheme of Work
2. Basic Science and Technology textbook
3. Teacher’s Guide
4. Relevant teaching materials
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Look around your school. You may see pupils, teachers, trees, flowers, grass, birds and insects.
Some of these things are living things. Living things can grow and need food, water and air.
MEANING OF LIVING THINGS
Living things are things that are alive.
Living things can:
1. grow;
3. breathe;
3. need food and water; and
4. reproduce.
For Primary 1 pupils, we can simply say: Living things are things that are alive.
EXAMPLES OF LIVING THINGS
Examples of living things are:
- Human beings
- Dogs
- Cats
- Birds
- Goats
- Fish
- Trees
- Flowers
- Grass
- Insects
LIVING THINGS IN THE SCHOOL ENVIRONMENT
There are many living things in the school environment.
1. People
2. Pupils
3. Teachers
4. School workers
5. Plants - Trees, Flowers, Grass and other smaller plants
5. Animals - Birds, Ants, Butterflies, Lizards and other smaller animals
CARING FOR LIVING THINGS
We should care for living things.
We can:
1. Water plants.
2. Avoid breaking tree branches.
3. Avoid killing harmless animals.
4. Keep the school environment clean.
5. Give animals proper care when they are kept as pets.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
Multiple Choice Questions
1. What are living things?
A. Things made of wood
B. Things that are broken
C. Things that are alive
2. Which of these is a living thing? A. Stone B. Tree C. Chair
3. Which of these is an animal? A. Book B. Table C. Dog
4. Which of these is a plant? A. Pencil B. Flower C. Cup
5. Which living thing can we see in school? A. Bird B. Spoon C. Bag
6. A pupil is a ______ thing. A. living B. non-living C. wooden
7. Which of these is a living thing? A. Ruler B. Desk C. Ant
8. What should we do to a plant? A. Break it B. Water it C. Step on it
9. Which of these can grow? A. Tree B. Stone C. Chair
10. Which of these is found in a school environment? A. Plate B. Flower C. Shoe
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. B 3. C 4. B 5. A
6. A 7. C 8. B 9. A 10. B
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that living things are things that are alive. They learned that people, plants and animals are examples of living things.
Pupils also learned that living things can be found in the school environment. They learned that we should care for plants and animals and keep the school environment clean.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pupils pictures of a person, a tree and a bird and asks them to identify them.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils look at the pictures and name the things they see.
Step 2: Meaning of Living Things
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains that living things are things that are alive.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils repeat the meaning of living things.
Step 3: Examples of Living Things
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of people, plants and animals.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils name the living things shown.
Step 4: Living Things in the School
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher asks pupils to mention living things they can see in the school.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention pupils, teachers, trees, flowers, birds, ants and other living things.
Step 5: Identifying Living Things
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of living and non-living things and asks pupils to identify the living things.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils point to and name the living things.
Step 6: Caring for Living Things
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains simple ways of caring for plants and animals.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways of caring for living things, such as watering plants and keeping the environment clean.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Name five living things.
- Group 2: Name three plants found in the school.
- Group 3: Name three animals found in the school.
- Group 4: Mention three ways to care for living things.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, identify, name and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the meaning and examples of living things and living things found in the school. The teacher gives pupils a different set of simple questions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and say what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
The teacher reminds pupils that people, plants and animals are living things. Pupils should care for living things and keep their school environment clean.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Living things are things that are alive. We can find many living things in our homes and around our homes.
People, plants and some animals are living things. They need food, water and air to live.
LIVING THINGS AT HOME
Some living things that can be found at home include:
1. People - Father, Mother, Brother, Sister and Other family members
2. Plants - Flowers, Grass, Trees, Potted plants
3. Animals - Dog, Cat, Chicken, Fish, Bird
CHARACTERISTICS OF LIVING THINGS
Living things have some important characteristics.
1. Living Things Grow - Living things grow bigger as they get older.
For example, a baby grows into a child, and a small plant grows into a bigger plant.
2. Living Things Need Food - Living things need food to grow and stay healthy.
People and animals eat food. Plants make their own food using sunlight, air and water.
3. Living Things Need Water - People, animals and plants need water to live.
4. Living Things Breathe - People and animals breathe air. Plants also carry out respiration.
5. Living Things Reproduce - Living things can produce young ones or new plants.
For example, a dog can have puppies and a plant can produce new plants.
6. Living Things Move - People and animals can move from one place to another. Plants can also show movement, such as turning towards light.
For Primary 1 pupils, remember: Living things grow, need food, need water, breathe, reproduce and move.
CARING FOR LIVING THINGS AT HOME
We should care for living things at home.
We can:
1. Give pets food and clean water.
2. Water plants.
3. Keep animals in a clean place.
4. Avoid hurting animals.
5. Keep the home environment clean.

A. Step on them
B. Water them
C. Break them
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. C 3. A 4. B 5. C
6. B 7. C 8. A 9. A 10. B
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that people, plants and animals are living things that can be found at home. They learned examples such as family members, flowers, trees, dogs, cats, chickens and fish.
Pupils also learned that living things grow, need food and water, breathe, reproduce and move. They learned that living things should be cared for properly.

Step 5: Other Characteristics

Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention examples of living things that breathe, move and produce young ones.
Step 6: Caring for Living Things

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Look around the classroom and your home. You will see many things such as chairs, tables, books, cups, bags and spoons.
These things are non-living things. They are not alive.
MEANING OF NON-LIVING THINGS
Non-living things are things that are not alive.
Non-living things do not grow, breathe, eat food or produce young ones.
Examples include: book, chair, table, pencil, cup, spoon, bag, shoe, stone, toy
EXAMPLES OF NON-LIVING THINGS
Some examples of non-living things are:
- Book
- Pencil
- Chair
- Table
- Bag
- Ruler
- Cup
- Spoon
- Shoe
- Toy
NON-LIVING THINGS IN THE CLASSROOM
We can find many non-living things in the classroom.
Examples are: chairs, tables, books, pencils, rulers, school bags, chalk, board, eraser, desks
NON-LIVING THINGS AT HOME
We can also find many non-living things at home.
Examples are: bed, chair, table, cup, spoon, plate, television, radio, bucket, cooking pot
LIVING AND NON-LIVING THINGS
Living things are alive, while non-living things are not alive.
Living Things - Child, Dog, Bird, Tree, Flower
Non-Living Things - Chair, Tables, Books, Pencils, Cup
Living things grow and need food, water and air. Non-living things do not grow or need food and water to live.

SUMMARY
Pupils learned that non-living things are things that are not alive. Examples include books, chairs, tables, pencils, cups, bags and stones.

2. Mention some types of energy.

4. State some uses of energy at home and in school.
5. Mention simple ways to use energy safely.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have seen and used things that need energy, such as light bulbs, fans, televisions and cooking appliances.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
Pictures or real objects of a bulb, fan, battery, torch, candle, cooking stove and solar panel.
METHOD OF TEACHING
The teacher uses observation, demonstration, questioning, discussion, identification, explanation, repetition and simple practical activities.
The teacher begins by showing pupils familiar objects such as a torch, bulb, fan and battery and asking them what the objects need to work.
REFERENCE MATERIALS

3. Teacher’s Guide
4. Relevant charts and pictures
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Energy helps us to do work and use many things around us. We need energy to see, move, cook, play and use some machines.
For example, a bulb needs energy to produce light, while a fan needs energy to turn its blades.
MEANING OF ENERGY
Energy is the ability to do work.
In simple words, energy helps us to do things.
We use energy every day at home, in school and in other places.
TYPES OF ENERGY
There are different types of energy. Some common types are:
1. Light energy - helps us to see.
2. Heat energy - makes things warm or hot.
3. Sound energy - helps us to hear sounds.
4. Electrical energy - powers electrical appliances.
5. Movement energy - is energy from moving things.
SOURCES OF ENERGY
Energy comes from different sources.
Examples include:
- The sun
- Electricity
- Batteries
- Fire
- Food
- Moving water
- Wind
USES OF ENERGY
We use energy for many things.
At Home
Energy is used to:
- Produce light.
- Cook food.
- Watch television.
- Listen to the radio.
- Use a fan.
- Charge phones.
- Iron clothes.
- Keep some food cold in a refrigerator.
At School
Energy is used to:
- Provide light in classrooms.
- Use computers.
- Use fans.
- Operate projectors.
- Ring electric bells.
- Charge some devices.
EXAMPLES OF ENERGY AND THEIR USES
Type of Energy - Use
1. Light energy - Helps us to see
2. Heat energy - Helps us to cook and keep warm
3. Sound energy - Helps us to hear
4. Electrical energy - Powers electrical appliances
5. Movement energy - Helps things move
SAFE USE OF ENERGY
We should use energy carefully.
1. Do not touch electrical wires.
2. Do not put fingers into electrical sockets.
3. Do not play with fire.
4. Do not touch hot objects.
5. Switch off lights and appliances when they are not needed.
6. Tell an adult when there is an electrical problem.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT

1. Energy helps us to ______.
A. sleep only
B. do things
C. hide

A. draw a line
B. read a book
C. cook food
4. Which of these uses electrical energy? A. Stone B. Fan C. Pencil
5. Which of these is a source of energy? A. Sun B. Book C. Ruler
6. Sound energy helps us to ______. A. write B. cook C. hear
7. A battery can provide ______ energy. A. electrical B. food C. sound
8. We use energy at home to ______.
A. grow chairs
B. cook food
C. make books
9. We should not play with ______. A. fire B. paper C. toys
10. We should switch off electrical appliances when they are ______. A. clean B. new C. not needed
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. B 3. C 4. B 5. A
6. C 7. A 8. B 9. A 10. C
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that energy helps us to do things. Energy is needed for light, heat, sound, movement and the use of electrical appliances.
Pupils also learned that energy comes from sources such as the sun, electricity, batteries, fire, food, wind and moving water. We must use energy safely.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher asks pupils to mention things they use that need energy, such as a fan, bulb and television.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention things that need energy.
Step 2: Meaning of Energy
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains that energy helps us to do things and gives simple examples.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, repeat the meaning of energy and give examples.
Step 3: Types of Energy
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher introduces light, heat, sound, electrical and movement energy using pictures and simple examples.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name the types of energy.
Step 4: Sources of Energy
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of the sun, battery, fire, wind and other sources of energy.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name the sources of energy.
Step 5: Uses of Energy
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains how energy is used at home and in school.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention different uses of energy.
Step 6: Safe Use of Energy
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains simple safety rules for using electricity, fire and hot objects.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state ways to use energy safely.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Name three types of energy.
- Group 2: Name three sources of energy.
- Group 3: Mention three uses of energy at home.
- Group 4: Mention three safety rules for using energy.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils work in groups, discuss their tasks and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the meaning, types, sources and uses of energy and asks pupils simple questions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention what they learned.
CONCLUSION
Energy is important in our daily life. It helps us to do many things at home and at school. We should use energy carefully and safely.

INTRODUCTION
Energy is important in our daily life. We need energy to see, move, cook food, keep warm and use some machines.

A source of energy is where energy comes from.
Common sources of energy include:
1. The Sun - gives us light and heat.
2. Food - gives people and animals energy to move and work.
3. Electricity - powers bulbs, fans, televisions and other electrical appliances.

3. Watch television.

We use energy to:

Energy comes from different sources and helps us to do many things. We use energy every day at home and at school. We should use energy carefully and safely.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Light is important in our daily life. It helps us to see things around us.
During the day, the sun gives us light. At night or in dark places, we can use sources such as electric bulbs, torches and lanterns to give us light.
MEANING OF LIGHT
Light is a form of energy that helps us to see.
Without enough light, it is difficult to see objects clearly.
For example, we can see our books clearly when there is enough light.
NATURAL SOURCES OF LIGHT
Natural sources of light are sources of light that occur naturally.
Examples include:
- The Sun - the main natural source of light during the day.
- Stars - give light in the night sky.
- Lightning - produces a bright flash of light during a storm.
- Fire - can occur naturally, although people also make fire.
ARTIFICIAL SOURCES OF LIGHT
Artificial sources of light are sources of light made or produced by people.
Examples include:
- Electric bulb
- Torch
- Lantern
- Candle
- Rechargeable lamp
- Street light
NATURAL AND ARTIFICIAL SOURCES OF LIGHT
- Natural Sources - Sun, Stars, Lightning, Natural Fire
- Artificial Sources - Electric Bulb, Torch, Candle, Lantern
IMPORTANCE OF LIGHT
Light is important because it:
1. Helps us to see.
2. Helps us to read and write.
3. Helps us to move around safely.
4. Helps us to find things.
5. Helps people to work at night.
8. Helps plants to grow.
9. Makes places bright.
LIGHT AT HOME AND SCHOOL
- At home, we use light from bulbs, torches and lamps to see and do our work.
- At school, light helps pupils to read books, write in their exercise books and see the teacher and board clearly.
SAFE USE OF LIGHT SOURCES
We should use light sources safely.
1. Do not look directly at very bright light.
2. Do not touch a hot bulb.
3. Do not play with candles.
4. Do not play with electrical wires.
5. Keep candles away from clothes and other things that can burn.
6. Ask an adult for help when using candles or electrical appliances.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
Multiple Choice Questions
1. Light helps us to ______. A. eat B. sleep C. see
2. Which of these is a natural source of light? A. Torch B. Sun C. Bulb
3. Which of these is an artificial source of light? A. Star B. Sun C. Electric bulb
4. The sun gives us ______. A. light B. books C. water
5. Which of these can help us to see at night? A. Torch B. Spoon C. Plate
6. Which is a natural source of light? A. Candle B. Star C. Lantern
7. Which is an artificial source of light? A. Lightning B. Sun C. Torch
8. Light helps pupils to ______.
A. read and write
B. grow taller
C. make food
9. We should not play with ______. A. pencils B. books C. candles
10. The main natural source of light for the Earth is the ______. A. Sun B. Moon C. cloud
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. B 3. C 4. A 5. A
6. B 7. C 8. A 9. C 10. A
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that light is a form of energy that helps us to see. The sun, stars and lightning are examples of natural sources of light, while bulbs, torches, candles and lanterns are artificial sources.
Pupils also learned that light helps us to read, write, work and move safely. Light sources should be used carefully and safely.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher switches on a torch or shows a bulb and asks pupils what the light helps them to do.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the light and say that it helps them to see.
Step 2: Meaning of Light
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains that light is a form of energy that helps us to see.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, repeat the meaning and give examples.
Step 3: Natural Sources of Light
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of the sun, stars and lightning and explains that they are natural sources of light.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name natural sources of light.
Step 4: Artificial Sources of Light
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures or real objects such as a torch, bulb, candle and lantern.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name artificial sources of light.
Step 5: Importance of Light
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains how light helps us to see, read, write, work and move safely.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways light helps them at home and school.
Step 6: Safe Use of Light
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains simple safety rules for using candles, bulbs and electrical appliances.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state ways to use light sources safely.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Name three natural sources of light.
- Group 2: Name three artificial sources of light.
- Group 3: Mention three importance of light.
- Group 4: Mention three safety rules for using light sources.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils work in groups, discuss their tasks and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the meaning, sources and importance of light and asks pupils simple questions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention what they learned.
CONCLUSION
Light is a form of energy that helps us to see. It comes from natural and artificial sources. We should use light sources carefully and safely.

Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is light?
2. Mention two natural sources of light.
3. Mention three artificial sources of light.
4. State three importance of light.
5. Mention two safety rules for using light sources.

topics.title: Water: Meaning and Sources of Water, and Distinguishing Water from Other Liquids | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 9 Basic Science and Technology
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (BST)
PRIMARY 1 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 9
THEME - WATER
PREVIOUS LESSON - Light Energy: Meaning of Light, Natural and Artificial Sources of Light, and Importance of Light | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 8 Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - WATER
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Sources of Water
3. Uses of Water and Other common liquids
4. Differences between water and other liquids
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of water.
2. Mention common sources of water.
3. State some uses of water.
4. Identify some other common liquids.
5. Distinguish water from other liquids by simple observations.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils use water every day for drinking, bathing, washing and other activities.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
Clean water in a transparent cup, pictures of a river, rain, well and tap, and pictures or samples of milk, cooking oil and fruit juice.
METHODS OF TEACHING
The teacher uses observation, demonstration, questioning, discussion, identification, comparison, explanation, repetition and simple practical activities.
The teacher begins by showing pupils a transparent cup of clean water and asking them what it is and where they can get water.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Lagos State Scheme of Work
2. Basic Science and Technology textbook for Primary 1
3. Teacher’s Guide
4. Relevant charts and pictures
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Water is very important to people, animals and plants. We use water every day for drinking, cooking, bathing, washing and other activities.
Water is a liquid. It can flow from one place to another and takes the shape of its container.
MEANING OF WATER
Water is a clear liquid that people, animals and plants need to live.
Clean water is safe for drinking when it has been properly treated or is from a safe source.
Water has no fixed shape. It takes the shape of the container in which it is kept.
SOURCES OF WATER
We get water from different sources.
Examples include:
- Rain - rain gives us water from the sky.
- River - rivers contain flowing water.
- Stream - streams are sources of water.
- Well - water can be obtained from wells.
- Borehole - boreholes provide underground water.
- Lake - lakes contain water.
- Tap - taps provide water for use in homes and schools.
USES OF WATER
We use water to:
1. Drink.
2. Cook food.
3. Bathe.
4. Wash clothes.
5. Wash plates.
6. Clean our homes.
7. Water plants.
8. Give animals water.
OTHER COMMON LIQUIDS
Apart from water, there are other liquids around us.
Examples include:
1. Milk
2. Cooking oil
3. Fruit juice
4. Soft drinks
5. Liquid soap
6. These liquids are different from water.
DISTINGUISHING WATER FROM OTHER LIQUIDS
We can distinguish water from other liquids by observing their colour, smell, taste and use. We should not taste an unknown liquid.
Liquid - Simple Observation
1. Water - Usually clear and has no strong smell
2. Milk - Usually white
3. Cooking oil - Usually oily and may be yellowish
4. Fruit juice - Usually coloured and has a fruit smell
5. Liquid soap - Usually coloured or scented and used for washing
Water is different from other liquids because it is usually clear, has no strong smell and is commonly used for drinking, cooking and washing.
WATER SAFETY
We should keep water clean.
1. Drink clean and safe water.
2. Keep drinking water covered.
3. Do not throw rubbish into water.
4. Wash hands before handling drinking water.
5. Do not drink water from an unknown or unsafe source.
6. Do not taste unknown liquids.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
Multiple Choice Questions
1. Water is a ______. A. solid B. stone C. liquid
2. Which of these is a source of water? A. Chair B. River C. Book
3. We use water for ______. A. drinking B. writing C. reading
4. Which of these is another liquid? A. Milk B. Pencil C. Table
5. Water is usually ______. A. black B. clear C. solid
6. Which of these provides water in many homes? A. Bag B. Shoe C. Tap
7. Cooking oil is different from water because cooking oil is ______. A. a book B. a stone C. oily
8. We use water to ______ plants. A. break B. water C. paint
9. We should keep drinking water ______. A. clean B. dirty C. open to rubbish
10. We should not taste ______.
A. our food
B. clean water
C. unknown liquids
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. B 3. A 4. A 5. B
6. C 7. C 8. B 9. A 10. C
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that water is a liquid that people, animals and plants need to live. Water comes from sources such as rain, rivers, streams, wells, boreholes, lakes and taps.
Pupils also learned that water is different from other liquids such as milk, cooking oil and fruit juice. Water should be kept clean and safe for use.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pupils a cup of clean water and asks them to identify it and mention where they get water.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the water, identify it and mention sources of water.
Step 2: Meaning of Water
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains that water is a liquid needed by people, animals and plants.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, repeat the meaning and give examples of how they use water.
Step 3: Sources of Water
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of rain, rivers, wells, boreholes, lakes and taps.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name the sources of water.
Step 4: Uses of Water
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher discusses common uses of water at home and school.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they use water every day.
Step 5: Other Liquids
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures or samples of milk, cooking oil, fruit juice and liquid soap.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the liquids and describe what they observe.
Step 6: Distinguishing Water from Other Liquids
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher guides pupils to compare water with other liquids by observing their colour, smell and common uses. The teacher reminds pupils not to taste unknown liquids.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe and state simple differences between water and other liquids.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Name three sources of water.
- Group 2: Mention three uses of water.
- Group 3: Name three liquids other than water.
- Group 4: State three differences between water and other liquids.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils work in groups, discuss their tasks and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the meaning, sources and uses of water and how to distinguish water from other liquids.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer questions and mention what they learned.
CONCLUSION
Water is an important liquid needed by people, animals and plants. It comes from different sources and is used for many activities. We should keep water clean and avoid tasting unknown liquids.
NEXT LESSON
Water: Properties and Uses of Water, and Importance of Water to Living Things | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 10 Basic Science and Technology
LESSON EVALUATION
1. What is water?
2. Mention three sources of water.
3. Mention three uses of water.
4. Name two liquids other than water.
5. State two ways water is different from other liquids.

topics.title: Water: Properties and Uses of Water, and Importance of Water to Living Things | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 10 Basic Science and Technology
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (BST)
PRIMARY 1 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 10
THEME - WATER
PREVIOUS LESSON - Water: Meaning and Sources of Water, and Distinguishing Water from Other Liquids | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 9 Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - WATER
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Properties and Uses of Water
3. Importance of water to people, Plants and Animals
4. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Mention some properties of water.
2. State some uses of water.
3. Explain why people need water.
4. Explain why animals need water.
5. Explain why plants need water.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that water is a liquid, its common sources and how it is different from other liquids.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
A transparent cup or bottle of clean water, a bowl, pictures of people, animals and plants, and simple objects for demonstrating water.
METHODS OF TEACHING
The teacher uses observation, demonstration, questioning, discussion, identification, comparison, explanation, repetition and simple practical activities.
The teacher begins by showing pupils a transparent cup of water and asking them to describe what they can see and mention some things they use water for.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Lagos State Scheme of Work
2. Basic Science and Technology textbook for Primary 1
3. Teacher’s Guide
4. Relevant charts and pictures
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Water is very important to life. People, animals and plants all need water to live and grow.
We use water every day at home, in school and in other places.
PROPERTIES OF WATER
Properties are the things we can observe about something.
Some simple properties of water are:
1. Water is a liquid.
2. Water is usually clear.
3. Water has no fixed shape. It takes the shape of its container.
4. Water flows.
5. Clean water has no strong smell.
6. Clean water has no taste.
For example, water in a cup takes the shape of the cup. When it is poured into a bowl, it takes the shape of the bowl.
USES OF WATER
We use water for many things.
At Home
Water is used for:
1. Drinking.
2. Cooking food.
3. Bathing.
4. Washing clothes.
5. Washing plates.
6. Cleaning the house.
7. Watering plants.
At School
Water is used for:
1. Drinking.
2. Washing hands.
3. Cleaning classrooms.
4. Washing school toilets.
5. Watering plants.
Other Uses
Water is also used for:
1. Giving animals water.
2. Farming.
3. Washing vehicles.
4. Some industrial activities.
IMPORTANCE OF WATER TO LIVING THINGS
Water is important to all living things.
Importance to People
People need water to:
1. Drink.
2. Stay healthy.
3. Cook food.
4. Keep the body clean.
5. Wash clothes and other things.
Importance to Animals
Animals need water to:
1. Drink.
2. Stay healthy.
3. Grow.
4. Help their bodies work properly.
Importance to Plants
Plants need water to:
1. Grow.
2. Stay fresh.
3. Make food.
4. Remain healthy.
WATER AND LIVING THINGS
Living Things - Why It Needs Water
People - Drinking, cooking and cleaning
Animals - Drinking and staying healthy
Plants - Growing and making food
KEEPING WATER CLEAN
We should keep water clean and safe.
1. Keep drinking water covered.
2. Do not throw rubbish into water.
3. Do not drink dirty water.
4. Use clean containers for storing water.
5. Keep wells and other water sources clean.
5. Tell an adult if water looks dirty or unsafe.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
Multiple Choice Questions
1. Water is a ______. A. book B. stone C. liquid
2. Water has no fixed ______. A. shape B. colour C. name
3. Water can ______ from one place to another. A. sleep B. flow C. sit
4. We use water for ______. A. drinking B. writing C. reading
5. People need water to stay ______. A. dry B. dirty C. healthy
6. Animals need water to ______. A. read B. drink C. write
7. Plants need water to ______. A. talk B. grow C. walk
8. We use water at school to ______.
A. wash our hands
B. break chairs
C. tear books
9. We should keep drinking water ______. A. clean B. dirty C. open
10. Which of these is a property of water?
A. It flows.
B. It is a chair.
C. It is a book.
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. A 3. B 4. A 5. C
6. B 7. B 8. C 9. A 10. A
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that water is a liquid that is usually clear, flows and has no fixed shape. Water takes the shape of the container in which it is kept.
Pupils also learned that water is used for drinking, cooking, washing, cleaning and farming. People, animals and plants need water to live and grow.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pupils a cup of water and asks them to describe what they can see and mention what they use water for.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the water and mention its uses.
Step 2: Properties of Water
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher demonstrates that water is a liquid, flows and takes the shape of its container.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the demonstration and describe the properties of water.
Step 3: Uses of Water
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains how water is used at home, school and other places.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention different uses of water.
Step 4: Importance to People
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains why people need water for drinking, cooking, cleaning and staying healthy.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state why people need water.
Step 5: Importance to Animals and Plants
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher shows pictures of animals and plants and explains why they need water.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify how animals and plants use water.
Step 6: Keeping Water Clean
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains simple ways to keep water clean and safe.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways to keep water clean.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Mention three properties of water.
- Group 2: Mention three uses of water.
- Group 3: State three reasons people need water.
- Group 4: State why animals and plants need water.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils work in groups, discuss their tasks and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the properties, uses and importance of water and asks pupils simple questions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention what they learned.
CONCLUSION
Water is very important to all living things. It has simple properties such as flowing and taking the shape of its container. We use water for many activities and should always keep it clean and safe.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Mention three properties of water.
1. State three uses of water.
2. Why do people need water?
3. Why do animals need water?
4. Why do plants need water?

topics.title: Movement: Practical Demonstration of Moving Our Body Parts Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 2 Physical and Health Education
topics.content:
PHYSICAL AND HEALTH EDUCATION (PHE)
PRIMARY 1 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME - BASIC MOVEMENTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Movement: Moving Our Body Parts | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 1 Physical and Health Education
TOPIC - PRACTICAL DEMONSTRATION OF MOVING OUR BODY PARTS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Body Movement
3. Practical Demonstration of Body Movements - Simple Movement Activities
4. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Identify body parts that can move.
2. Demonstrate simple movements of different body parts.
3. Follow simple movement instructions.
4. Mention some benefits of body movement.
5. Demonstrate movements safely.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils can identify common body parts such as the head, arms, hands, legs, knees and feet.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Body-part charts or pictures
2. Whistle
3. Open playground or classroom space
METHODS OF TEACHING
The teacher uses observation, demonstration, questioning, identification, imitation, repetition, discussion and simple practical activities.
The teacher begins by asking pupils to stand up and demonstrate simple movements such as raising their hands, bending their knees and moving their feet.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Lagos State Scheme of Work
2. Physical and Health Education textbook for Primary 1
3. Teacher’s Guide
4. Relevant charts and pictures
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Our body parts can move in different ways. We use our body parts to walk, run, jump, bend, stretch, clap and play.
Practical movement activities help pupils understand how different body parts move.
BODY PARTS USED FOR MOVEMENT
The following body parts can move:
- Head
- Neck
- Arms
- Hands
- Fingers
- Waist
- Legs
- Knees
- Feet
- Toes
PRACTICAL DEMONSTRATION OF BODY MOVEMENTS
1. Moving the Head
Pupils can gently move their heads:
- Up and down.
- From side to side.
2. Moving the Arms
Pupils can:
- Raise their arms.
- Lower their arms.
- Stretch their arms.
- Swing their arms gently.
3. Moving the Hands
Pupils can:
- Clap their hands.
- Open and close their hands.
- Wave their hands.
4. Moving the Fingers
Pupils can:
- Bend and straighten their fingers.
- Move their fingers one at a time.
- Wiggle their fingers.
5. Moving the Waist
Pupils can gently:
- Bend forward.
- Bend backward slightly.
- Turn their body from side to side.
6. Moving the Legs
Pupils can:
- Lift one leg.
- Bend their knees.
- Stretch their legs.
- Walk.
- Run slowly.
7. Moving the Feet
Pupils can:
- Move their feet forward and backward.
- Stand on one foot briefly.
- Walk and jump gently.
SIMPLE MOVEMENT ACTIVITIES
The teacher gives simple instructions for pupils to follow:
1. Stand straight.
2. Raise both hands.
3. Lower both hands.
4. Clap three times.
5. Bend your knees.
6. Stretch your arms.
7. Walk forward.
8. Walk backward carefully.
9. Jump gently.
10. Stand still.
IMPORTANCE OF BODY MOVEMENT
Body movement:
1. Exercises the body.
2. Keeps the body active.
3. Makes muscles stronger.
4. Helps us move from one place to another.
5. Helps us play and take part in activities.
6. Helps us control our body.
SAFETY DURING PRACTICAL ACTIVITIES
Pupils should:
1. Exercise in a safe and open space.
2. Follow the teacher’s instructions.
3. Avoid pushing other pupils.
4. Avoid running into other pupils.
5. Move gently.
6. Wear suitable clothing and footwear.
7. Stop when the teacher says so.
8. Tell the teacher if they feel pain or get injured.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
Multiple Choice Questions
1. Which body part can we raise? A. Ear B. Hand C. Nose
2. We use our legs to ______. A. see B. smell C. walk
3. Which of these is a movement? A. Sitting quietly B. Sleeping C. Clapping
4. We can move our head ______.
A. by eating
B. from side to side
C. by writing
5. Which body part can we bend? A. Knee B. Eye C. Ear
6. We use our hands to ______. A. clap B. smell C. hear
7. Body movement helps to keep us ______. A. dirty B. active C. weak
8. During movement activities, we should not ______ other pupils. A. greet B. help C. push
9. Movement activities should be done in a ______ place. A. crowded B. dangerous C. safe
10. When the teacher says stop, we should ______.
A. stop moving
B. run away
C. push others
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. C 3. C 4. B 5. A
6. A 7. B 8. C 9. C 10. A
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that different parts of the body can move in different ways. They practised moving their heads, arms, hands, fingers, waist, legs, knees and feet.
Pupils also learned that movement helps to exercise the body and keep it active. They should follow instructions and move safely during practical activities.
PRESENTATION
Step 1: Introduction
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher asks pupils to stand and gently move their hands, heads and legs.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils stand and follow the teacher’s instructions.
Step 2: Identifying Body Parts
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher points to different body parts and asks pupils to identify them.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name the body parts.
Step 3: Demonstration of Head and Arm Movements
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher demonstrates moving the head from side to side and raising, lowering and stretching the arms.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils imitate the movements.
Step 4: Demonstration of Hand and Finger Movements
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher demonstrates clapping, waving and moving the fingers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils practise the movements.
Step 5: Demonstration of Leg and Foot Movements
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher demonstrates bending the knees, walking, jumping and moving the feet.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils practise the movements carefully.
Step 6: Movement Instructions
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher gives simple movement instructions such as “raise your hands,” “clap,” “bend your knees” and “jump gently.”
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen and perform each movement.
Step 7: Group Activity
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Demonstrate three head and neck movements.
- Group 2: Demonstrate three arm and hand movements.
- Group 3: Demonstrate three leg and foot movements.
- Group 4: Demonstrate three simple whole-body movements.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its activities.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils work in groups, practise the movements and present their activities.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the body movements demonstrated and asks pupils simple questions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and demonstrate selected movements.
CONCLUSION
Different parts of our body can move in different ways. We can raise, bend, stretch, clap, walk, run and jump. We should always perform movement activities safely.
NEXT LESSON
Movement (Throwing and Kicking): Meaning and Practical Demonstration of Throwing and Kicking of Objects | Primary 1 (Basic 1) First Term Week 3 Physical and Health Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Mention four body parts that can move.
2. Demonstrate two movements of the hands.
3. Demonstrate two movements of the legs.
4. Mention two benefits of body movement.
5. State two safety rules during movement activities.
